slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Koko nearly toppled over putting on a sock. Good news: balance isn't set in stone. It's a skill, and it tends to improve with regular practice.

Balance relies on strength, knowing where your body is, and reacting quickly. Pilates trains your trunk, hips and legs together, and standing work on the reformer lets you practise with springs and a bar for support.

Try this today: hold the kitchen bench lightly and stand on one foot for 20–30 seconds. As it gets easier, use one finger, then none. Swap sides. If you've had recent falls or feel dizzy, check with your GP or physio first.

Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physio can build a balance program that starts where you are. Book online via the link in bio.
